facts.statement: Zaraapelta was a herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Zaraapelta is an extinct genus of herbivorous ankylosaurid thyreophoran dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The species Zaraapelta nomadis was named and described by Arbour and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: The type species is Zaraapelta nomadis, named and described by Arbour et al in 2014.

facts.statement: The holotype skull was discovered in 2000 by Robert Gabbard in the Gobi Desert near Hermiin Tsav.
facts.quote: In 2000, Robert Gabbard, member of a team headed by Philip John Currie, found an ankylosaur skull in the Gobi Desert near Hermiin Tsav at the Baruungoyot.

facts.statement: The genus name Zaraapelta combines the Mongolian word for 'hedgehog' and the Greek word for 'small shield' to reflect the animal's prickly armor.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Mongolian , "hedgehog", in reference to the prickly appearance of ankylosaurs, and the Greek πέλτη, , "small shield", a common component of ankylosaurian names in view of their body armour.

facts.statement: The species name 'nomadis' refers to the Nomadic Expeditions travel agency that organized the fossil-hunting trips to Mongolia.
facts.quote: The specific name is the genitive of the Latin , "nomad" and refers to the Nomadic Expeditions travel agency that has organised many palaeontological expeditions to Mongolia.

facts.statement: The fossil record consists of a skull missing the snout tip, with no lower jaw elements found.
facts.quote: It consists of a skull lacking the snout tip. No elements of the lower jaws were discovered.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the single known specimen likely represents a subadult individual.
facts.quote: The specimen probably represents a subadult individual.

facts.statement: Zaraapelta is unique among ankylosaurs for having a squamosal horn with a smooth upper cutting edge that abruptly transitions to a rough surface on the sides.
facts.quote: Zaraapelta differs from all other Ankylosauria in the possession of a squamosal horn with a very smooth bone texture along the upper cutting edge, abruptly changing into a rough surface at the inner and the outer side

facts.statement: The squamosal horn located at the top rear of the skull is robust and pyramid-shaped.
facts.quote: The squamosal horn, on the top rear corner of the skull, is robust and pyramid-shaped.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Zaraapelta as the closest relative to the genus Tarchia.
facts.quote: It was found to be closest to Tarchia in the phylogenetic analysis within its description.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses have recovered Zaraapelta as the sister species of Tarchia.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis recovered it as the sister species of Tarchia.

facts.statement: Zaraapelta lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian stage, about 70 million years ago in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Zaraapelta nomadis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Zaraapelta es un género extinto de dinosaurio tireóforo anquilosáurido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 70 millones de años durante el Maastrichtiense en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the abundance of ankylosaurs like Zaraapelta in the area was due to sufficient vegetation to support multiple herbivore populations, though their specific ecological niches remain unclear.
facts.quote: She assumed that this relative ankylosaurian abundance in species had been caused by their being the main herbivores in the area, enough crop thus being available to feed three populations, although their relative niches were unclear.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that the distinct head ornamentation of Zaraapelta served for species recognition.
facts.quote: The differences in head ornamentation would then have served species recognition.

facts.statement: It is assumed that sexual selection played a role in the evolution of Zaraapelta's unique head ornamentation.
facts.quote: However, she also assumed that sexual selection had been a factor in the evolution of the typical Zaraapelta head ornamentation.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding whether Zaraapelta is a distinct species or an older individual of Tarchia with shifted bone structures, but authors reject this due to lack of similar ontogenetic changes in other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: It might thus in principle be possible that Zaraapelta simply represents an old Tarchia individual in which this osteoderm has shifted on top of the squamosal horn, creating the strange double-layered structure. This possibility was rejected by the authors however, because from other ankylosaurian species no comparably large ontogenetic changes of the squamosal horn shape are known.

facts.statement: Zaraapelta was a medium-sized ankylosaur with a preserved skull measuring about 40 centimeters in length without the premaxillae.
facts.quote: El cráneo conservado tiene, sin los praemaxilares, tiene una longitud de unos 40 centímetros, lo que indica que Zaraapelta era un anquilosaurio de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: Zaraapelta is unique among all ankylosaurs for having a squamosal horn with a very smooth bone texture along its upper cutting edge.
facts.quote: Zaraapelta se diferencia de todos los demás Ankylosauria en la posesión de un cuerno escamoso con una textura ósea muy suave a lo largo del borde cortante superior

facts.statement: The squamosal horn of Zaraapelta is robust and pyramid-shaped, located at the upper rear corner of the skull.
facts.quote: El cuerno escamoso, en la esquina superior trasera del cráneo, es robusto y tiene forma de pirámide.

facts.statement: The cheek area behind the eye socket of Zaraapelta features flat osteoderms separated by deep grooves, creating a delicate "dry mud" pattern.
facts.quote: El área de la mejilla entre estos grandes cuernos, detrás de la cuenca del ojo, está llena de osteodermos planos, separados por surcos profundos, que crean un delicado patrón de "barro seco".

facts.statement: The only known species, Zaraapelta nomadis, was named and described by Arbour et al. in 2014.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida es Z. nomadis, nombrada y descrita por Arbour et al. in 2014.

facts.statement: Zaraapelta is known from a single fossil skull found in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: Zaraapelta es conocido a partir de un único cráneo fósil hallado en la Formación Nemegt de Mongolia.

facts.statement: The skull of Zaraapelta was discovered in 2000 by Robert Gabbard, a member of a team led by Philip John Currie, in the Gobi Desert near Hermiin Tsav in Baruungoyot.
facts.quote: En 2000, Robert Gabbard, miembro de un equipo liderado por Philip John Currie, halló un cráneo de anquilosaurio en el desierto de Gobi cerca de Hermiin Tsav en Baruungoyot.

facts.statement: The genus name Zaraapelta is derived from the Mongolian word "zaraa," meaning "porcupine," referring to the spiny appearance of ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del mongol zaraa, "puercoespín", en referencia a la apariencia espinosa de los anquilosaurios

facts.statement: The species name nomadis is the genitive of the Latin word "nomas," meaning "nomad," referring to the Nomadic Expeditions travel agency that organized many paleontological expeditions to Mongolia.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, nomadis es el genitivo del latín nomas, "nómada" y se refiere a la agencia de viajes Nomadic Expeditions (expediciones nómadas) que ha organizado muchas expediciones paleontológicas a Mongolia.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a skull missing the tip of the snout, and no jaw elements were discovered.
facts.quote: Consiste de un cráneo que el falta la punta del hocico. No se descubrieron elementos de las mandíbulas.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is likely that of a subadult individual.
facts.quote: Probablemente este espécimen corresponde a un individuo subadulto.

facts.statement: Zaraapelta is classified within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Zaraapelta se colocó en los Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis recovered Zaraapelta as the sister species to Tarchia.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico la recuperó como especie hermana de Tarchia.

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Zaraapelta is estimated from the Cenomanian to the Santonian stages, between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researcher Arbour noted that Saichania, Tarchia, and Zaraapelta shared the same habitat.
facts.quote: Arbor señaló que Saichania, Tarchia y Zaraapelta compartían el mismo hábitat.

facts.statement: It was assumed that the relative abundance of ankylosaur species was caused by them being the main herbivores in the area, providing enough food for three populations.
facts.quote: Se asumió que esta abundancia relativa de especies de anquilosaurios había sido causada por ser los principales herbívoros en el área, por lo que había suficiente cosecha disponible para alimentar a tres poblaciones

facts.statement: Differences in head ornamentation likely served for species recognition among these ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Las diferencias en la ornamentación de la cabeza habrían servido entonces para el reconocimiento de especies.

facts.statement: Sexual selection was also assumed to be a factor in the evolution of the typical head ornamentation of Zaraapelta.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, también asumió que la selección sexual había sido un factor en la evolución de la ornamentación típica de la cabeza de Zaraapelta.

facts.statement: Researchers rejected the hypothesis that Zaraapelta might represent a larger individual of Tarchia with a shifted accessory osteoderm, because comparable large ontogenetic changes in squamosal horn shape are unknown in other ankylosaur species.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, esta posibilidad fue rechazada por los autores, porque de otras especies de anquilosaurios no se conocen cambios ontogenéticos comparablemente grandes de la forma del cuerno escamoso.
